prompt.extractFieldBool: (boolean true/false; checked/yes in the image means true, fill false when uncertain)
prompt.extractFieldEnum: (must be one of: {values}; leave empty when uncertain)
prompt.extractGroupLine: - {key} ({title}): array, each element represents one row of the table, fields:
prompt.extractGroupsHead: You are an information extraction assistant. The user's screenshots may contain [one or more] tables listed below. First determine which tables actually appear in the images, then extract every data row of each table into a JSON object. Output strictly one single JSON object whose keys are table names and values are row arrays; return an empty array [] for tables not present in the images. Do not output any explanation, prefixes, suffixes or code fences. Table definitions:
prompt.extractGroupsTail: Requirements: extract only data rows that truly exist in the images, never fabricate; header rows and placeholder rows (e.g. 'no data yet') are not data rows; fill an empty string for unrecognized fields (false for boolean fields). Table data may not appear as regular tables: if the images contain merged cells or free text paragraphs of remarks/notes whose content clearly maps to a table's fields (e.g. mentioning a .sql script file name and an owner implies the database scripts table), split them into rows of that table as well, leave unmapped fields empty and put remaining notes into a remarks field; still never fabricate. Pay special attention to [row-spanning merged cells]: if a cell in a column visually spans multiple rows, its content applies to all those rows, so fill the same value for that field in each of those rows; strictly judge which row each column's content belongs to by the vertical boundaries of each row, and never shift content to adjacent rows.
prompt.extractSingleHead: You are an information extraction assistant. Extract information from the user's screenshots and output strictly one single JSON object,
prompt.extractManyHead: You are an information extraction assistant. The user's screenshots may contain [multiple] records (e.g. a list or table). Extract each record in the images into a JSON object and output strictly one single JSON array,
prompt.extractFieldsIntro: do not output any explanation, prefixes, suffixes or ```json code fences. Field definitions:
prompt.extractSingleTail: Requirements: the JSON keys must match the definitions above; fill an empty string "" for fields that cannot be recognized from the images; never fabricate content that does not exist in the images.
prompt.extractManyTail: Requirements: the keys of every array element must match the definitions above; extract only entries that truly exist in the images, never fabricate; fill an empty string for unrecognized fields. Pay special attention to [row-spanning merged cells]: if a cell in a column visually spans multiple rows, its content applies to all those rows, so fill the same value for that field in each of those rows; strictly judge which row each column's content belongs to by the vertical boundaries of each row, and never shift content to adjacent rows.
prompt.extractHintSingle: Extract the fields above from this screenshot and return JSON only.
prompt.extractHintMany: Extract every record in the screenshots as an array element and return a JSON array only.
prompt.extractHintGroups: Identify the tables in the screenshots and extract every row grouped by table; return a JSON object only.
prompt.snippetExtractHint: This is a screenshot containing commands/SQL/tables/config/text, possibly with multiple entries. Extract every entry that can be saved as a snippet into one record (title, category and content).
prompt.problemExtractHint: This is a screenshot of production issues/tickets/meetings/messages, possibly with multiple entries. Extract each entry into one record (issue title, type and note).
prompt.problemAnalysisIntro: You are a senior backend/full-stack engineer. Analyze the following production issue and answer entirely in English.
prompt.problemAnalysisAsk: Based on the description, please provide: 1. possible root-cause directions (ranked by likelihood), 2. investigation steps (logs, SQL, API verification), 3. fix suggestions.
prompt.repairSystem: You are a JSON repair assistant. The user will give you a JSON text with format errors. Fix syntax errors (missing or extra quotes / commas / brackets, single quotes, trailing commas, comments, unescaped characters, Python-style True/False/None, etc.) and make it valid JSON while preserving the original data and structure as much as possible. Do not add, remove, or fabricate field values. Strictly output only the repaired JSON itself, with no explanation, prefix/suffix, or ```json code fence.
prompt.mockSystem: You are a test data generation assistant. The user will give you a JSON as a structural template and a generation requirement. Generate brand-new, realistic-looking fictional mock data: ①keep the template's field names and hierarchy unchanged by default, only replace field values; ②values must match the semantics of the field names (e.g. name is a person name, email is an email, date is a date) and keep the same value types; ③if the user asks for multiple items, a different count, or added/removed fields, adjust accordingly; ④never use real personal information (real phone numbers / ID cards / bank cards), use clearly fictional samples. Strictly output only the generated JSON itself, with no explanation, prefix/suffix, or ```json code fence.
prompt.mockDefaultReq: Keep the original structure, generate one new reasonable sample.
prompt.presetGeneral: You are a helpful developer assistant. Answer accurately and concisely; use Markdown fenced code blocks for code.
prompt.presetRegex: You are a regular expression expert. Generate a regex from the user's description and briefly explain each part.
prompt.presetCodeExplain: You are a senior developer. Explain the code the user pasted: purpose, key implementation points, potential issues, and improvement suggestions.
prompt.presetPolish: You are a copywriting expert. Polish the user's text, keep the original meaning, use a natural and professional tone, and output only the polished result.
prompt.presetTestData: You are a test data generation assistant. Generate realistic-looking fictional data as requested; never use real private information.
prompt.dbDialectMysql: MySQL dialect: backticks for identifiers (e.g. `user`); LIMIT n OFFSET m for paging; single quotes for strings; AUTO_INCREMENT for auto-increment columns; `?` placeholders; supports IFNULL, DATE_FORMAT, GROUP_CONCAT.
prompt.dbDialectPostgres: PostgreSQL dialect: double quotes for identifiers (lowercased when unquoted); LIMIT n OFFSET m for paging; single quotes for strings; SERIAL/IDENTITY for auto-increment columns; ::type casts; supports COALESCE, to_char, STRING_AGG; booleans TRUE/FALSE; no AUTO_INCREMENT or IFNULL.
prompt.dbDialectSqlite: SQLite dialect: double quotes for identifiers; single quotes for strings; INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT for auto-increment columns; LIMIT n OFFSET m for paging; no RIGHT JOIN or FULL JOIN; date functions use date()/strftime(); loose type affinity.
prompt.dbDialectOracle: Oracle dialect: double quotes for identifiers (uppercased when unquoted); single quotes for strings; no LIMIT, paging must use FETCH FIRST n ROWS ONLY or ROWNUM; IDENTITY or sequences for auto-increment columns; string concatenation with {'|'}{'|'}; empty strings are treated as NULL; pseudo-column ROWNUM; dates use TO_DATE/TO_CHAR.
prompt.dbGenSqlSystem: You are a senior DBA and SQL expert. Generate one SQL statement from the user's requirement, output only the SQL itself with no explanation, prefix/suffix, or code fence.
prompt.dbExplainSystem: You are a senior DBA. The user will give you the database type (if not given, infer from the SQL itself), a SQL statement, and an error message. Explain the cause of the error, point out the exact problem, and provide fixed SQL if needed. Keep it concise.
prompt.dbOptimizeSystem: You are a senior DBA. Analyze the user's SQL: point out potential performance issues (full table scans, missing indexes, N+1 queries, unnecessary round-trips, etc.), give actionable optimization advice, and rewrite the SQL when necessary. Strictly follow the target dialect when rewriting; do not switch to MySQL syntax. Output in bullet points, keep it concise.
prompt.iconGenSystem: You are an app icon designer. Strictly return one complete SVG only, no explanation and no Markdown code fence. The SVG must use viewBox="0 0 512 512", centered composition, clear outlines, few tiny elements, and stay recognizable at 32px. Forbidden: text, images, scripts, CSS, filters, gradients, masks, external links, foreignObject and use; use only path, circle, rect, line, polyline, polygon, ellipse, g and basic fill/stroke attributes.

mobile.shellIntro: The mobile app is being rebuilt. This build confirms three things: platform detection, the native bridge and the translation catalogue. Feature screens land module by module.
mobile.bridgeOn: Native bridge connected (files, HTTP and the keystore come from the app)
mobile.bridgeOff: No native bridge: running as a web page (data in local IndexedDB, AI direct)
mobile.nativeOff: Running in a browser (used for development and automated tests)
mobile.tabTodo: This module is still being ported; screens land one module at a time.
mobile.workNoIteration: No iterations yet. Create one, then attach requirements.
mobile.workNoSubtask: No subtasks on this requirement yet.
mobile.noteDb: Android has no JDBC: SQLite files only (MySQL / PostgreSQL / Oracle need the desktop build).
mobile.noteNetwork: Android WebView has no ICMP or raw sockets: only TCP reachability checks remain; ping/traceroute/DNS are out of scope.
mobile.noteLabel: Android has no Windows RAW print queue: layout, preview and .prn export work; sending to a printer needs a TSPL-capable tool. Requires the app.
mobile.noteDownloader: Android has no arbitrary-path writes, so multi-GB chunks have nowhere to land or be merged: the multi-threaded downloader is desktop-only for now.
mobile.noteCheckin: Android has no equivalent of a resident tray or launch-at-startup, so a scheduled daily check-in makes no sense here; signing in from the web page is quicker anyway
mobile.noteNetcapture: Capturing means connecting to a local debug port and launching the target process, neither of which Android can do: the app either is not on the phone or runs on another device.
mobile.convertBase64Note: Base64 treats input as UTF-8; decode failures usually mean the content is not UTF-8 text (binary images, for example).
mobile.cryptoLocalNote: Everything is computed on this device; nothing is uploaded.
mobile.genMockNote: Pick fields (defaults to the first three) to generate fake data you can paste straight into API debugging.
mobile.reqNoHeaders: No headers yet. Tap + above to add one.
mobile.reqCorsNote: Inside the app, requests go out over native HTTP (no CORS restrictions, same as desktop). When previewed in a browser they use fetch and are subject to the target site CORS policy.
mobile.imgLocalNote: Everything is processed on this device; images are never uploaded.
mobile.setDensityNote: Compact is the phone default; Comfortable increases line height and spacing for one-handed or large-screen use.
mobile.setStorageNote: Data stays on this device (the app's private storage). It only leaves the device when cloud sync is on, and the server only ever sees ciphertext.
mobile.setKeyUnreadable: Could not decrypt the stored key: {err}. The keystore may have been reset, or this value is plaintext left by an older version. Re-enter the API key and save; leaving the field blank keeps the stored value.

skillReason.run_not_found: That run record no longer exists.
skillReason.run_not_skillable: This run cannot become a skill yet: it needs a successful tool call and complete enough steps.
skillReason.not_reusable: Semantic matching thinks this is a one-off. Tap the same run again to save it anyway.
skillReason.invalid: The extracted skill was invalid and was skipped.
skillReason.unknown: This run cannot be turned into a skill right now.

mobile.pdfLocalNote: Everything is processed on this device; PDFs are never uploaded.
mobile.netTcpNote: Port check: inside the app this is a real TCP handshake (same as desktop); when previewed in a browser it degrades to reachability probing and only covers web ports.
mobile.noteFile: Android has no arbitrary-path file access: files must be authorised through the system picker (SAF). Requires the app.
mobile.setUpdateNote: Reads a fixed update manifest and compares versions; when a new build exists it is downloaded, verified, then handed to the system installer. Android has no silent updater like desktop, so the install confirmation still comes from the system.
mobile.setUpdate_web: The web build always serves the latest version—just refresh the page. Installing or upgrading needs the Android app.
mobile.setUpdateFailedHint: If this is a network error: the APK is downloaded from GitHub—check that the phone can reach GitHub, then retry later.
mobile.setUpdate_available: New version {version} is available to download and install.
mobile.setUpdate_invalid: The update manifest is unavailable (not published yet, or the URL changed). This is NOT "up to date" — don't treat it as no update.
mobile.setUpdate_unknown: This build can't read its package version (normal in the web preview), so no comparison is possible.
mobile.setUpdate_installing: Handed to the system installer — please confirm the dialog.
mobile.setUpdate_need_permission: Allow "install unknown apps" first: we opened the system settings page; tap download and install again afterwards.
mobile.fileNeedApp: File access requires the app (browser previews have no system file picker).
mobile.fileSafNote: Android has no arbitrary-path file access: the file must first be authorised through the system picker. The grant lasts for this installation.
mobile.fileLossy: This file contains bytes that could not be decoded and are shown as replacement characters — the content may be incomplete.
mobile.dbNeedApp: Database access requires the app (browser previews have no SQLite).
mobile.dbSqliteOnly: Android has no JDBC: only SQLite files are supported here (MySQL / PostgreSQL / Oracle need the desktop build).
mobile.dbFilePh: Filled in after choosing a file; you can also type an app-accessible path
mobile.dbTruncated: Too many rows — showing the first {n}. Add LIMIT or WHERE to narrow it down.
mobile.dbNoTables: This database has no tables yet.
mobile.dbNeedFile: Choose or enter a SQLite file first.
mobile.labelNoPrint: Android has no Windows RAW print queue: this generates the TSPL commands and preview, and you send the exported .prn with a TSPL-capable print tool. Layout uses the same engine as desktop, so what you see is what gets printed.
mobile.chatLocalNote: Messages go only to the AI endpoint you configured; no plaintext copy is kept on this device (sessions live in app-private storage).
mobile.setBackupNote: A backup packs all local data into a JSON file and downloads it (keep it in cloud storage or copy it to a computer). Restoring picks that file through the system picker — desktop zip backups cannot be restored here.
mobile.setBackupEmpty: There is no data to back up yet.
mobile.setRestoreNotJson: This is not a phone backup (desktop backups are zip files — restore those on a computer).
mobile.setRestoreBad: This is not a valid phone backup.
mobile.setRestoreBad_wrongFormat: Backup format mismatch — this may be a JSON file from another tool.
mobile.setRestoreBad_notBackup: No backup marker in this file.
mobile.setRestoreBad_noVersion: The backup has no version, so its format cannot be confirmed.
mobile.setRestoreBad_tooNew: This backup comes from a newer app version; update first.
mobile.setRestoreBad_noEntries: The backup contains no data entries.
mobile.ovNoLogs: No hours or logs recorded yet.
mobile.setCapsNote: What works on the phone and what differs from desktop. Items marked unavailable are Android platform limits, not unfinished work.
mobile.capNo_jdbc: Android has no JDBC (the database tool supports SQLite only)
mobile.capNo_rawPrint: Android has no Windows RAW print queue (export .prn and send it with a print tool)
mobile.capNo_multiWindow: No multiple windows on phones (tools are full-screen pages)
mobile.capNo_autostart: Launch-at-startup does not apply to mobile
mobile.capNo_updater: Updates are installed by the system; no in-app updater
mobile.capNo_localFile: Android has no arbitrary path access (files go through the system picker)
mobile.capNo_icmp: No ICMP or raw sockets in WebView (TCP reachability checks remain)
mobile.domainEmpty: No domains yet. Domains group code repositories (pools).
mobile.domainRemoveMsg: Delete “{name}”? Its pools will be deleted too.
mobile.poolEmpty: No pools in this domain yet.
mobile.poolPathNote: The path is only recorded; the phone never accesses it (no local repositories on Android).
mobile.releaseDeployNote: “Auto” infers from the name prefix (names starting with online are treated as containers).
mobile.releaseDup: A release pool named “{name}” already exists.
mobile.releaseNote: The phone only **records and shows release state**: real packaging and deployment happen on the build machine (Android has no local repositories or build environment).
mobile.setSelfTestNote: Tap once after installing to verify each native capability (storage, local server, TCP, encryption, file picker, SQLite). Checks that need a file are not run automatically — run them individually. You can copy the report afterwards.
mobile.checkManual: Needs a picked file — run it with the button
mobile.noteScreenshot: Screenshots rely on global hotkeys, full-screen capture and always-on-top pin windows, which Android does not offer; the phone's built-in screenshot tools are a better fit.
mobile.noteDisk: Disk analysis walks the whole local directory tree (hundreds of thousands of entries) and aggregates it natively; Android has no equivalent scope — use the system storage settings instead.
mobile.notePrompt: The prompt tool needs a local ComfyUI and desktop-native capabilities (streaming writes, system player); not available on Android.
